questions.question: When a traffic signal light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, you must let pedestrians and other traffic finish crossing the intersection.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time. Which one must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right when both arrive at the same time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is on top and green is on bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: You see two solid yellow lines on the road. When can you cross them?

options.text: Only to turn left into an alley, driveway, or private road.
To pass other vehicles if no traffic is coming.
Never.
Only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into an alley, driveway, or private road.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing. You can only cross them to turn left into an alley, driveway, or private road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: You turn left onto a one-way street. Which lane should you end up in?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the direction you came from.

questions.question: You must pull over for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Go through slowly and carefully.
Get ready to stop because the light will turn red soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and check both directions before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Which action does NOT make night driving safer?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see at night.
Keep a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking at oncoming headlights will make your eyes contract. When the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back. During this time, you cannot see the road well.

questions.question: A vehicle is coming toward you with high beams on. Where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by the headlights. This way you can still see the road and stay in your lane until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for the police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: Move your vehicle off the road if possible after a minor accident. Always tell others who you are and offer help.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
Traffic moves in one direction only.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not need to stop.
Slow down to check that cross traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the nearest point to the intersection where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar place, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you drive.
Just know roughly where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you drive.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance before driving to an unfamiliar place. Check the location on a map before you start driving.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle when stopping?

options.text: On a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space when stopped on an uphill slope. This helps prevent a collision if the vehicle in front rolls backward when traffic starts moving.

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Yes, it lowers your blood alcohol level.
Yes, it cancels out the alcohol.
No, it has no effect on your blood alcohol level.
No, it raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it has no effect on your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. While it may help you stay awake, it cannot make you sober or change how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.question: What does a pennant-shaped sign mean?

options.text: School zone.
No passing zone.
Speed limit.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text confirming it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination sooner.
Drive closer to the car in front.
Stay farther behind the car in front.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between your vehicle and the car in front when driving on wet roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming up. Watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to let any train pass before you cross.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to let any train pass before you cross.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to let trains pass before you cross the tracks, especially when there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your whole vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not change gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph could take up to ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers need more distance to stop than regular cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph needs almost 400 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down when entering, speed up when leaving.
Keep the same speed the whole way through.
Speed up when entering, slow down when leaving.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when entering, speed up when leaving.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve and increase speed gradually as you leave. If you speed up entering a curve, your vehicle will be harder to control.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: If you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only during an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only during an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to continue driving in your current direction.

questions.question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same once you are on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: This is a rule sign that drivers must always follow. When you see this sign, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or in one place.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or in one place.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be in one place or moving, like vehicles marking lines, mowing grass, or removing snow. Orange signs with black letters mark work zones. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A train station is ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains pass.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. Always slow down at a railroad crossing. Trains cannot move out of your way, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to go after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, check the other track for another train before you go.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check the other track for another train before you go.
questions.explanation: When there are two tracks, watch for a second train after the first one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track.
